summary: Pine County steel tower erected 1935 (86 ft); ten women hired for tower work in 1945; listed as standing; current access not documented.

events.note: ten women hired for tower jobs that season because of a manpower shortage; one was Ada Noeldner of Bruno

evidence.supports: photo caption: erected 1935 at the Nickerson Forestry Station
evidence.quote: Erected in 1935 at the Nickerson Forestry Station.

evidence.supports: tower on the highest point of land between the Twin Cities and Duluth (1945 item)
evidence.quote: The Nickerson tower is located on the highest point of land between the Twin Cities and Duluth

evidence.supports: ten women hired for tower jobs in 1945 because of a manpower shortage
evidence.quote: Mrs. Ada Noeldner of Bruno one of ten women hired for tower jobs this season because of the manpower shortage

evidence.supports: Noeldner took the post while waiting for her husband to return from the Ninth Army
evidence.quote: to await the return of her husband Harold with the Ninth Army in Germany

evidence.supports: eight hours a day spent watching the distant landscape
evidence.quote: spends eight hours a day watching for suspicious smudges on the distant landscape

evidence.supports: 1945 item attributed to the Askov American

notes_for_editor: Central page and Commons caption agree on 1935 and 86 feet; height_m 26.2 is the metric conversion of 86 ft and matches the brief. No source found on who built the tower, why, its current access, or current staffing, so no access or staffing key is written. The Central page also prints a code 45N-17W-9 under the county name; not used. Two WebSearch hits (a 1928 Nimrod tower in Wadena County and a 1935 Pequot Lakes tower) are different structures and were not used. Record agency is null and stays null.
